Built for LLM Memory with 120 minute pacing. Readiness 90/100 with 1 validation issue(s).

LLM Memory Instructor Preview

Duration: 120 minutes

Audience: 40% beginner / 60% advanced

Curriculum Plan

| Module | Objective | Minutes | Difficulty | |---|---|---:|---:| | Working Memory vs Long-Term Memory | Differentiate context-window memory from persisted memory stores in LLM systems. | 15 | 25% | | Context Windows and Compression | Explain why context limits require summarization and memory compression strategies. | 19 | 38% | | Embeddings, Indexing, and Retrieval Intent | Connect embeddings and vector indexes to memory recall quality. | 25 | 52% | | Memory Read/Write Policies | Design explicit policies for what to store, when to update, and when to forget. | 28 | 62% | | Agent Memory Architecture in Practice | Implement memory retrieval and persistence hooks in a deterministic agent workflow. | 33 | 75% |

Script
1. Working Memory vs Long-Term Memory

Teach Working Memory vs Long-Term Memory through this objective: Differentiate context-window memory from persisted memory stores in LLM systems.. Ground the explanation with one technical claim from official docs and one failure mode.

Beginner layer: Beginner framing: Frame memory as two layers: transient context in the current prompt and persisted memory retrieved on demand. Misconception to preempt: Teams treat every user message as long-term memory, causing irrelevant context bloat and response drift. Use one concrete analogy and short glossary callout.

Advanced layer: Advanced challenge tied to Working Memory vs Long-Term Memory. Trade-off prompt using prerequisite chain: none. Include one architecture trade-off and mitigation strategy.

Interaction: Given a support chatbot, identify one fact that belongs in working memory and one that belongs in long-term memory.

Transition: Before moving on, ask learners how Working Memory vs Long-Term Memory changes implementation choices.

2. Context Windows and Compression

Teach Context Windows and Compression through this objective: Explain why context limits require summarization and memory compression strategies.. Ground the explanation with one technical claim from official docs and one failure mode.

Beginner layer: Beginner framing: Show how finite context windows force trade-offs between recency, relevance, and completeness. Misconception to preempt: A summarizer drops user constraints, so the assistant repeatedly violates the same preference. Use one concrete analogy and short glossary callout.

Advanced layer: Advanced challenge tied to Context Windows and Compression. Trade-off prompt using prerequisite chain: memory-types. Include one architecture trade-off and mitigation strategy.

Interaction: Ask learners to choose what to keep, summarize, or drop from an overlong chat transcript.

Transition: Before moving on, ask learners how Context Windows and Compression changes implementation choices.

3. Embeddings, Indexing, and Retrieval Intent

Teach Embeddings, Indexing, and Retrieval Intent through this objective: Connect embeddings and vector indexes to memory recall quality.. Ground the explanation with one technical claim from official docs and one failure mode.

Beginner layer: Beginner framing: Convert memory entries into vectors and query by semantic similarity to recall relevant history. Misconception to preempt: Low-quality chunking stores fragments without context, returning misleading partial memories. Use one concrete analogy and short glossary callout.

Advanced layer: Advanced challenge tied to Embeddings, Indexing, and Retrieval Intent. Trade-off prompt using prerequisite chain: context-window. Include one architecture trade-off and mitigation strategy.

Interaction: Have learners compare lexical keyword matching vs embedding retrieval for the same query.

Transition: Before moving on, ask learners how Embeddings, Indexing, and Retrieval Intent changes implementation choices.

4. Memory Read/Write Policies

Teach Memory Read/Write Policies through this objective: Design explicit policies for what to store, when to update, and when to forget.. Ground the explanation with one technical claim from official docs and one failure mode.

Beginner layer: Beginner framing: Introduce write filters, deduplication, decay, and conflict handling to keep memory usable over time. Misconception to preempt: No deduplication leads to repeated contradictory entries and unstable responses. Use one concrete analogy and short glossary callout.

Advanced layer: Advanced challenge tied to Memory Read/Write Policies. Trade-off prompt using prerequisite chain: embeddings-and-index. Include one architecture trade-off and mitigation strategy.

Interaction: Ask learners to draft one write rule and one delete rule for a personal-assistant bot.

Transition: Before moving on, ask learners how Memory Read/Write Policies changes implementation choices.

5. Agent Memory Architecture in Practice

Teach Agent Memory Architecture in Practice through this objective: Implement memory retrieval and persistence hooks in a deterministic agent workflow.. Ground the explanation with one technical claim from official docs and one failure mode.

Beginner layer: Beginner framing: Wire memory read before generation and memory write after response with validation checkpoints. Misconception to preempt: Memory writes happen before response validation, persisting hallucinated details as facts. Use one concrete analogy and short glossary callout.

Advanced layer: Advanced challenge tied to Agent Memory Architecture in Practice. Trade-off prompt using prerequisite chain: memory-read-write. Include one architecture trade-off and mitigation strategy.

Interaction: Have learners map memory read/write points onto a request lifecycle diagram.

Transition: Before moving on, ask learners how Agent Memory Architecture in Practice changes implementation choices.

Script
1. Working Memory vs Long-Term Memory

Teach Working Memory vs Long-Term Memory through this objective: Differentiate context-window memory from persisted memory stores in LLM systems.. Ground the explanation with one technical claim from official docs and one failure mode.

Beginner layer: Beginner framing: Frame memory as two layers: transient context in the current prompt and persisted memory retrieved on demand. Misconception to preempt: Teams treat every user message as long-term memory, causing irrelevant context bloat and response drift. Use one concrete analogy and short glossary callout.

Advanced layer: Advanced challenge tied to Working Memory vs Long-Term Memory. Trade-off prompt using prerequisite chain: none. Include one architecture trade-off and mitigation strategy.

Interaction: Given a support chatbot, identify one fact that belongs in working memory and one that belongs in long-term memory.

Transition: Before moving on, ask learners how Working Memory vs Long-Term Memory changes implementation choices.

2. Memory Read/Write Policies

Teach Memory Read/Write Policies through this objective: Design explicit policies for what to store, when to update, and when to forget.. Ground the explanation with one technical claim from official docs and one failure mode.

Beginner layer: Beginner framing: Introduce write filters, deduplication, decay, and conflict handling to keep memory usable over time. Misconception to preempt: No deduplication leads to repeated contradictory entries and unstable responses. Use one concrete analogy and short glossary callout.

Advanced layer: Advanced challenge tied to Memory Read/Write Policies. Trade-off prompt using prerequisite chain: embeddings-and-index. Include one architecture trade-off and mitigation strategy.

Interaction: Ask learners to draft one write rule and one delete rule for a personal-assistant bot.

Transition: Before moving on, ask learners how Memory Read/Write Policies changes implementation choices.
